blurb:
She greeted volunteers at the front desk of the shelter. That's the kind of dog Monica is. One year old, about 35 pounds, friendly with people and dogs, and she's already putting in volunteer hours while she waits for her family to show up.

Monica came from animal control and is currently going through Mostly Mutts' Prison Pups training program, so she's picking up skills while she's there. She's got separation anxiety, which she's not hiding from you, and she needs a home where someone is around most of the time. Work from home, retired, stay-at-home parent. If your house has someone in it most of the day, she's going to be great. She just needs to learn that when you leave, you're coming back. Mostly Mutts has a trainer who will actually help you with that after adoption, which is a real thing they offer.

She's also heartworm positive right now, but treatment is happening soon. That's why they're asking for local adoption only, which makes sense.

She does well with other dogs, so if you've already got a laid-back pup at home, that could actually make the separation anxiety easier on everyone. Kids 15 and up are a better fit since she gets excited and jumpy when little ones run.

Call Mostly Mutts at the number below to find out when Monica is available to meet. She's off-site for training, so timing matters.
shelter_hours: Call or check website for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Heartworm treatment, separation anxiety, and local-only restriction create real placement friction worth surfacing to find the right fit
• Greeting volunteers at the front desk is a rare, vivid detail that makes her instantly memorable in print
• Active prison training program and medical hold suggest she has been in the system long enough to need a targeted push

blurb:
She came from animal control, went through an immersive prison training program, got adopted, came back because her energy was too much for one family, and is now living in a foster home waiting for the right people to find her. That's Josie's whole story, and honestly it's not a sad one. It just means she needs someone who actually wants a dog that's up for things.

Josie is six years old, about 35 pounds, and has the kind of floppy ears and nubby tail that are genuinely hard to look at without smiling. She knows sit, stay, and come. She walks on a leash. She'll do zoomies when the mood hits and then fold herself onto the couch next to you like she was always there. Her energy runs between a 5 and a 7, which isn't exhausting if you like walks and outdoor time, but it was too much for her last family, so it's worth being honest with yourself about that before you go meet her.

She does best as an only dog, no cats, and probably kids 10 and older since she gets playful and mouthy sometimes. Never mean, just enthusiastic. If you've got an active household and room for a medium-sized hound mix who already knows the basics, she's ready right now.

Josie is in foster care through Mostly Mutts, which is in Kennesaw. Submit an inquiry through their website or call to set up a meeting.
shelter_hours: Call or check website for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Prison training program plus a return adoption is a layered, compelling arc that rewards reader attention
• Trained, leash-ready, and couch-ready — a genuinely practical package for active adopters who do their homework
• Returned once and now in foster waiting again, implying a meaningful stretch of unresolved placement

blurb:
Ten years old, nine pounds, and she just had a spay, a dental, and a mammary mass removal, all after coming out of a neglectful situation. Rae has had a rough stretch. But she's in foster care now, she's healing up, and by the accounts of the people taking care of her, she's doing just fine.

She's not a high-energy dog. Her days go something like this: nap, short walk, some exploring, collect a little petting, another nap. That's the routine and she likes it. She's not looking for a playmate and she's not going to follow you from room to room demanding attention. She's calm, curious, and friendly in a quiet way.

She's pretty hard of hearing, which means voice commands don't always land. Her foster gets her attention by tapping her leg, and Rae comes right to her. It's a small adjustment, not a big one. Mostly Mutts also offers free lifetime training for all their adopted dogs, so there's real support available if you want help figuring out what works for her.

She lives peacefully with other dogs in her foster home, basically ignoring them, so a calm resident dog is fine. Older kids who know to be gentle with a small senior are a good match.

If you want a small, quiet companion who just needs a soft place to land for the rest of her years, Rae is worth going to meet. She's at Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw.
shelter_hours: Call or check website for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Neglect survivor who just cleared major surgery — the emotional stakes for this senior are as high as it gets
• Low-maintenance, quiet companionship is an underserved niche that speaks directly to older or less active readers
• Senior age, medical history, and hard-of-hearing status all signal she is statistically the hardest placement here and the most urgent to feature

blurb:
Three months old, 4.5 pounds, and already running the room. Dionne came into Mostly Mutts after she and her sister were pulled from animal control. They did a stint in foster care, came back to the shelter, and apparently charmed every volunteer in the building. She's ready for a home of her own now.

She's curious, playful, and loves a good cuddle once she's burned through her energy. The pattern is pretty predictable: nap, recharge, play session, repeat. She gets along great with her sister and other cats she's met, so a household that already has a cat is a natural fit. Dogs are unknown, and there's no data on that yet, so a slow introduction would be smart if that's your situation.

One thing to know upfront: she hasn't been spayed yet because she's still a little small, but Mostly Mutts covers that cost with one of their approved vets in the North Metro Atlanta area. That means this is a local adoption only. The adoption fee is $175, her microchip is already in, and her kitten shots are started. You'll need to finish those as she grows.

Dionne is available through Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue. Submit an inquiry on their website to get the process going.
shelter_address: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue, Kennesaw, GA (North Metro Atlanta area)
scoring_notes:
• Local-adoption-only restriction and pending spay narrow the pool, making a newsletter spotlight strategically valuable
• Playful, cuddly kitten personality is reliably high-appeal for casual readers browsing the newsletter
• Animal control origin with a shelter bounce adds modest backstory weight without a standout hook

blurb:
At two and a half months old and barely a pound and a half, Emu already has her whole personality figured out. She and her siblings lost their mom at around five weeks old, and a good samaritan got them to Mostly Mutts before anything bad could happen. They landed in a foster home and have been going strong ever since.

Her foster mom describes the litter as pretty much perfect, which is a high bar, and Emu holds her own. What sets her apart from her siblings is that she's the independent one. Not aloof, just confident. She plays hard, chases mouse toys, tears through tunnels, and climbs things she probably shouldn't. Then she finds your lap and settles in. The foster home has other cats and a dog, and she hasn't been fazed by any of it.

She's litter trained, good with kids who handle cats gently, and adaptable around dogs as long as the dog is chill about cats. If you have another cat at home who could use a playmate, she's going to be a good fit. If you're starting from scratch, she's going to keep you entertained either way.

Emu is available through Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue. Visit their website to submit an inquiry and arrange a meet.
shelter_address: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue, Kennesaw, GA (North Metro Atlanta area)
scoring_notes:
• Orphaned kitten with a survival hook gives readers an immediate emotional entry point
• Broad compatibility — dogs, cats, kids, solo homes — makes her one of the easiest placements in this group
• Recently rescued and thriving in foster, suggesting minimal wait time and lower feature urgency

blurb:
This guy has been through more than most cats will ever see, and he still wants to sit in your lap. Peeta is a 5.5-year-old Domestic Shorthair/Siamese mix with a genuinely wild backstory: adopted as a kitten, returned when his family went through some life changes, adopted again, then rushed to emergency surgery after accidentally swallowing a string that wrapped around his tongue and worked its way into his GI tract. He made it through all of it. He's fully recovered and apparently unbothered.

What the volunteers will tell you is that he was shy when he came back to his foster home, which makes sense given everything. But he came around fast. Now he follows his foster around looking for attention and winds up underfoot anytime someone is nearby. He's not a cat who keeps his distance. He wants to be with you, and he will make that pretty clear.

He's litter trained, got along with other cats in his previous home, and would likely do fine with kids who know how to handle a cat. Dogs are unknown, so a meet and greet would be smart if you have one. He'd probably do best in a home where someone is around regularly, since affection is basically his whole thing.

Peeta is available through Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue. Head to their website to submit an inquiry and set up a visit.
shelter_address: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue, Kennesaw, GA (North Metro Atlanta area)
scoring_notes:
• Survived emergency GI surgery and two returns — a resilience narrative readers will rally behind
• Affectionate, lap-seeking personality makes him a strong emotional match for a wide adopter base
• Multiple rehoming cycles and adult age signal a long, difficult road that creates genuine urgency
